findings.reason: the node must perturb by more than the assertion's tolerance (minutes, as §27 did) or it cannot satisfy "fails on main" and the control reads as a passed check that never exercised the drift.
findings.text: §31's done-when says the test "fails on main under" moving the wall clock forward "a second between the two reads", but the drifting assertion is `budget_block["budget_age_s"] == pytest.approx(0, abs=1)` (`tests/test_picker_dispatch_pace.py:292`), whose tolerance is ±1 s: a one-second drift yields `budget_age_s == 1.0`, which the assertion accepts, so the control passes on main and measures nothing; §27's analogous control (its neighbour's `approx(7200, abs=1)`) used an hour, above its tolerance

findings.reason: a node that chooses the "show both" branch cannot satisfy the single done-when, so the section must either drop that branch or give it its own clause.
findings.text: §30 says "Make the block's headroom and the gate's verdict come from one figure, or show both in the block, so Jev never sees headroom the gate will refuse", but its done-when only measures the first branch ("every candidate the block presents with headroom passes the gate, and a candidate the gate refuses shows no headroom"): under the "show both" branch the block still presents the harness-independent headroom (`reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:234`, `_context_block`) for a candidate the per-backend gate (`routing._context_fit_verdict`) refuses, which is exactly the state the done-when forbids and the goal sentence calls out
